slides.title: Decomposing Financial Market Dynamics via Mechanism Analysis in an Evolutionary Multi-Agent Simulation
slides.highlight: This research identifies distinct control knobs for diversity, realism, and fragility in evolutionary multi-agent simulations, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: Distinct mechanisms in evolutionary agent-based markets act as separate control knobs for diversity, realism, and fragility.
card.key_idea: A simulator with 120 agents uses pluggable mechanisms to decompose effects: QD selection drives diversity/cycling, reflexive microstructure drives realism, and behavioral bias drives genomic fragility.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 3x20-seed interventions across three scenarios using sign-tests and bootstrap CIs. Results show robust separability, though some effects are only directionally positive.
card.limitation: Uses proxies for fragility and cycling; realism is limited to 5 facts; results are from a single simulator.

slides.title: Charting the Growth of Social-Physical HRI (spHRI): A Systematic Review Pipeline Augmented by Small Language Models
slides.highlight: This research explores using small language models to assist in screening literature for social-physical human-robot interaction, supporting the RwB goal of advancing embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Small Language Models (SLMs) can augment systematic reviews by recovering relevant papers missed by human reviewers.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using a unanimity ensemble of four locally deployed SLMs (≤1.5B parameters) as a second-pass filter for title and abstract screening in spHRI research.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 32,000 records against human labels. The SLM ensemble identified 39 additional relevant papers (10.29% of final set), screening orders of magnitude faster than humans.
card.limitation: SLMs cannot replace expert judgment due to a precision-recall tradeoff and currently provide binary outputs without confidence scoring.

slides.title: A Taxonomy of Conceptual Alignment in Human-Robot Dialogue
slides.tldr: TAXONOMY FOR CONCEPTUAL ALIGNMENT IN HRI
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a taxonomy and dialogue act schema for conceptual alignment in human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and HRI.

card.one_liner: A design-centric taxonomy and dialogue act schema for analyzing and designing conceptual alignment in human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Conceptual alignment is framed as a bidirectional, co-constructive process characterized by three initiation triggers, five levels of conceptual representation, and a structured set of dialogue acts.
card.evaluation: Developed via literature review and empirical analysis of 48 human-human dialogues (2,677 turns) in a collaborative image-sorting task.
card.limitation: Based on controlled human dialogues, potentially omitting in-the-wild dynamics and robotic constraints like perception or embodiment limitations.

slides.title: When Robots Rate Their Own Interactions: Engagement Validity and the Strangeness Failure
slides.highlight: This research explores inverted evaluation where LLM-powered robots rate their own interactions, showing moderate agreement on engagement but a failure to accurately assess strangeness. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and AI-mediated embodied learning.

card.one_liner: LLM-powered robots can accurately rate interaction engagement but systematically fail to detect human strangeness/discomfort.
card.key_idea: An 'inverted evaluation' framework where LLMs complete standardized HRI questionnaires from the robot's perspective using interaction transcripts and multimodal context.
card.evaluation: Tested via HRI-CUES dataset (5 LLMs, 1,522 evaluations) and a Nao robot pilot (N=4). Metrics included Pearson r and ICC.
card.limitation: LLMs lack access to internal affective states, conflating philosophical engagement with comfort and failing on unexpressed strangeness.

slides.title: ZUOWEI Unveils Humanoid Care Robots to Address Global Aging Challenges
slides.tldr: HUMANOID CARE ROBOTS FOR AGING POPULATIONS
slides.highlight: ZUOWEI has introduced humanoid care robots designed to address global aging challenges, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Real-Time Voice AI Hears but Does Not Listen
slides.highlight: This research identifies a disconnect between perception and action in real-time voice AI, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Real-time voice AIs prioritize spoken words over vocal delivery, ignoring critical emotional cues during decision-making.
card.key_idea: The 'emotional intelligence gap' occurs when models perceive distress or sarcasm in single-turn diagnostics but disregard those cues in multi-turn consequential scenarios.
card.evaluation: Four production systems (GPT Realtime 2, Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, Qwen3.5 Omni Plus/Flash) were tested using synthesized audio across scenario-based calls and diagnostics.
card.limitation: Prompting systems to attend to vocal delivery only partially and inconsistently improves performance, failing to fully close the gap.

slides.title: Predictive Gaze Is Preserved but Reorganized toward Monitoring during Robot-Mediated Manipulation
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that predictive gaze is preserved during robot-mediated manipulation but shifts toward monitoring the end-effector, providing a signal for inferring action intentions in human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: Predictive gaze is preserved during robot telemanipulation but shifts more toward monitoring the end-effector.
card.key_idea: Investigation of gaze behavior during goal-directed telemanipulation to determine how visuomotor control adapts to altered embodiment and disrupted sensorimotor coupling.

slides.title: Students' Perception Accuracy of Partners' AI Use and its Relation to Collaboration Performance
slides.highlight: This study examines how misaligned perceptions of a partner's AI use affect team performance, relating to HyECHO's focus on modeling engagement and team state in hybrid human-AI settings.

card.one_liner: Misaligned perceptions of partners' AI use correlate with lower final project scores in student collaborations.
card.key_idea: A longitudinal study analyzing how accuracy in perceiving a partner's generative AI usage affects collaborative programming performance and team outcomes.
card.evaluation: Three-wave longitudinal study of 103 student pairs in an introductory software engineering course; results linked perception misalignment to final project scores.
card.limitation: Perception misalignment does not consistently decrease through face-to-face pair-programming sessions.

slides.title: SupplyNet: Supporting Visual Exploratory Learning in Supply Chain via Contextual Multi-Agent Simulation
slides.highlight: SupplyNet utilizes a contextual graph-based LLM multi-agent framework to model interdependent dynamics, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: SupplyNet is a gamified visual simulation system for learning supply chain dynamics via LLM-driven multi-agent simulation.
card.key_idea: Combines a contextual graph-based LLM multi-agent framework with a branching timeline for "what-if" exploration and an interactive network view for causal tracing.
card.evaluation: User study comparing SupplyNet to a classic baseline simulation; participants reported increased engagement and perceived understanding of supply chain dynamics.

slides.title: voxmap-studio: An open-source speaker diarization annotation tool with built-in cost instrumentation
slides.highlight: This tool provides a framework for labeling speaker diarization data with built-in cost instrumentation, supporting the development of diarization and listener modeling for HyECHO.

card.one_liner: An open-source speaker diarization tool that treats annotation cost and effort as first-class recorded outputs.
card.key_idea: React-based tool featuring stride-accelerated automatic initialization, uncertainty-based segment highlighting, cost instrumentation (edit operations/time), and confirmation-gated exports with "phantom" attention checks to ensure ground-truth quality.
card.evaluation: Preliminary study on nine AMI audio files comparing manual vs. assisted annotation using editOps, time, and DER metrics.
card.limitation: Preliminary study used only one annotator and three files per condition, preventing broad statistical conclusions.

slides.title: STEB: A Speech-to-Speech Translation Expressiveness Benchmark for Evaluating Beyond Translation Fidelity
slides.highlight: This work introduces STEB to evaluate the preservation of emotion, scenario style, and nonverbal vocalizations in speech-to-speech translation, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: STEB is a benchmark evaluating expressiveness preservation (emotion, style, nonverbals) in Chinese-English speech-to-speech translation.
card.key_idea: A reference-free LLM-as-a-judge framework using a caption-then-summarize pipeline to compare structured expressive attributes of source and translated speech.
card.evaluation: Six S2ST systems were tested on 32.6 hours of audio. Results show strong translation fidelity but poor emotion and nonverbal preservation.
card.limitation: Currently limited to Chinese-English and depends on the captioning model's ability to perceive paralinguistic cues.

slides.title: BiPACE: Bisimulation-Guided Policy Optimization with Action Counterfactual Estimation for LLM Agents
slides.tldr: IMPROVED ADVANTAGE ESTIMATION FOR LLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: BiPACE introduces a bisimulation-guided policy optimization method that improves credit assignment for long-horizon LLM agents. This is relevant to MIMIC's use of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: BiPACE improves LLM agent training by refining step-level credit assignment using behavioral clustering and action-conditioned baselines.
card.key_idea: BiGPO clusters actor hidden-states via cosine distance to group behaviorally equivalent states, while PACE uses action-conditioned peer baselines to estimate a nonparametric Q-V advantage.
card.evaluation: Tested on ALFWorld, WebShop, and TextCraft using Qwen2.5 (1.5B/7B). BiPACE Q outperformed GiGPO, reaching 97.1% success on ALFWorld/7B with higher sample efficiency.
card.limitation: Evaluated only on text-only environments with discrete action spaces; uses a fixed cosine radius requiring one-time calibration.

slides.title: Do more heads imply better performance? An empirical study of team thought leaders' impact on scientific team performance
slides.tldr: IMPACT OF THOUGHT LEADERSHIP ON TEAM PERFORMANCE
slides.highlight: This study examines how the number of thought leaders affects team impact and disruptiveness, contributing to HyECHO's focus on understanding group norms and team states.

card.one_liner: More thought leaders in scientific teams have an inverted U-shaped effect on impact and reduce disruptiveness.
card.key_idea: Analyzes 140,000+ PLOS papers, defining thought leaders as authors responsible for conceptual tasks to measure their impact on team impact and disruptiveness.
card.evaluation: Correlational and causal analysis of 140,000+ PLOS journal papers; results examine team impact, disruptiveness, and interactions with size, gender, and international collaboration.
